items.title: Mickey Roker interviewed by Michael Woods, Majesty of the Seas, May 31, 1995
items.q: He used to play drums with Jimmy Smith. Great drummer man. He played with a lot of people.

ctx.x: Uh oh, uh oh, talk about polyrhythms.

But I didn’t know nothing about no polyrhythms back then you know. ‘Cause I was self taught you know, and I had never heard a waltz before you know. I mean not to know that it was a waltz. So anyway, the guys are turning around and looking at me man, and I’m wondering what’s wrong. Because the beat ain’t right, man, it ain’t matching up. So man that’s when I learned that there was a different rhythm other than four-four. But if I hadn’t gone to that jam session and put myself in a position like that, I never…

But that sense of readiness. You know you said something else about the jam sessions. You know when jazz first started moving into the colleges, a lot of administrators didn’t understand or even think that jam sessions were necessary.
